summary: Port of .rddev/dispatch harness behavior into rddev Go code, submitted for acceptance. Go implementation complete: registry with disk-only discovery + /proc starttime pid-reuse pairing (worker_registry.go), env credential stripping + neutralised GH_CONFIG_DIR (worker_env.go), task-package renderer + fail-closed schema validator (worker_render.go), guard/settings/reaper generation (worker_guard.go), spawn pipeline with one-per-task worktree lifecycle + parallelism gate (worker_spawn.go), stop (worker_stop.go), cmd/rddev worker CLI (worker.go). Canonical worker-guard.sh with 147-case two-sided regression suite (shellcheck-clean) and .rddev.example copy byte-identical (drift-tested). CLI integration suite 8/8 green with real separate processes: two concurrent workers in disjoint worktrees without cross-pollution, separate-process parentage, crash exit 3 / timeout exit 124 recorded never-completed, parallelism gate (default 3 / hard max 4, refused spawn starts nothing), restart-style disk discovery + stale detection, stop, 8 generated-guard two-sided probes. REAL-claude e2e (third run, /tmp/t0010-e2e-kiC8, log /tmp/t0010-e2e.log): two genuine claude -p workers ran concurrently and both produced complete RESULT.json + hello.txt byte-exact in their own scopes; T0001 exited 0, T0002 hit its hard $0.30 budget mid-final-turn (recorded exited-1, never completed — designed behavior); refs unchanged outside task/** and remotes/**; three isolation probes through the spawn-generated guard PASS (control-plane blocked, neighbour allowed, device write allowed); ps snapshot proves the workers are reaper children (bash run-worker.sh ppid 1 after rddev exited, claude -p as its child) — separate processes, no subagent. Three production bugs found and fixed with regression assertions: (1) gitOutput stringified *exec.ExitError with %s so branchExists could never see exit 1 (worktree creation broken on any repo without the task branch) — fixed %w + errors.As; (2) the --timeout wrapper was passed to claude as its FIRST ARGUMENT so timed-out workers were never killed — fixed by wrapping the full command in Spawn; (3) renderer emitted JSON null for nil slices, which the task-package schema rejects — fixed with strSlice normalization. Additionally the e2e exposed that the generated settings (Bash-only allow) denied the Write tool entirely in dontAsk mode; two real-claude probes proved claude 2.1.269 ignores path-scoped Write/Edit allow rules (absolute and env: forms both deny even allowed paths), while the dispatch harness demonstrably allows the Write tool (this Worker's own session runs its settings); the port now matches dispatch: bare Write/Edit allows, envelope enforced at the guard (shell writes) and collect-time allowed_scope diff (worktree), with a unit test forbidding dead path-scoped entries from reappearing. A third real-claude probe confirms Write works under the generated settings (2 files, 0 denials) and Edit is permitted (its only error was claude's own read-before-edit rule). Boundary with T0011 confirmed via task-state-machine.yaml command_mapping: T0010 = spawn/list/logs/stop + worktree lifecycle + registry + prompt renderer + guard generation; T0011 = collect validation.

acceptance.criterion: Two Workers for different tasks ran concurrently without sharing a writable tree.
acceptance.evidence: Supervisor verified from the worker's e2e artifact /tmp/t0010-e2e.log: T0001 (pid 334918) and T0002 (pid 334939) were spawned into disjoint worktrees with distinct run_ids and registries.

acceptance.criterion: The Worker is a separate Claude Code process, not a subagent.
acceptance.evidence: Supervisor verified from /tmp/t0010-ps-snapshot.txt: the nested worker appears as `claude -p --name worker-...` orphaned to pid 1 after rddev exited - no ancestor is a Claude session.

acceptance.criterion: After a Supervisor restart, running and stale workers are discovered from disk alone.
acceptance.evidence: Supervisor verified from the e2e log: a FRESH `rddev worker list` process reported both workers as exited with their exit_status read from the on-disk registry.

acceptance.criterion: A Worker crash/timeout is recorded as failed and never accepted as completed.
acceptance.evidence: Worker reported exit 3 (crash), 124 (timeout) and 1 (budget) all recorded as exited/failed with the task left running. Supervisor independently confirmed the timeout wiring is correct (the timeout binary precedes `claude`, not passed as its first argument) - a bug the worker found and fixed.

acceptance.criterion: The ported isolation is demonstrated two-sided.
acceptance.evidence: Supervisor ran tests/worker-guard/guard-regression.sh: 147/147 PASS, and spot-checked the exact cases from the hand-rolled harness - `git commit` blocked, `docker ps` blocked without a grant, while `grep -n docker docker-compose.yml` and `grep -rn service docs/` are ALLOWED (the two over-blocking bugs fixed in L1-20260912-13).

risks: Guard derives from documented harness behavior (tasks/decisions.md L1-20260912-3/9/13/16, T0011 isolation-smoke evidence, specs/orchestrator/worker-permissions.yaml, docs/61/63); .rddev/dispatch/* is permission-denied to this Worker. Divergence risk mitigated by the two-sided suite and real-claude isolation probes.

The Write/Edit tools are allowed bare (dispatch parity) and are NOT interceptable by the PreToolUse guard (matcher Bash|Read|Grep|Glob|NotebookRead, as in the dispatch harness). Out-of-scope worktree writes are caught at collect (T0011, allowed_scope diff); writes outside the repo are bounded only by worker instructions. Path-scoped Write allow rules would be the fix but claude 2.1.269 ignores them (probed) — see follow_up_issues.

go test ./... is red on tests/integration because local PostgreSQL (127.0.0.1:15432) is not running and this Worker has no Docker grant; the Supervisor's G3 environment should re-run it — the failing tests do not exercise T0010 code.
The e2e 'grep -v grep' artifact (worker argv contains 'grep' from the embedded prompt) is a note for future evidence scripts, not a product bug.
follow_up_issues: Supervisor: run scripts/spec_version.py --write to refresh specs/SPEC_VERSION.json after worker-registry.schema.json landed (CI spec-validation.yml --check is red until then).

T0011 (collect): consider a PostToolUse audit hook that rejects Write/Edit tool calls outside the shell-write envelope after the fact, since claude 2.1.269's PreToolUse matcher does not cover Write/Edit and path-scoped allow rules are ignored in dontAsk mode (probed 2026-09-12).

When a future claude version honors path-scoped Write/Edit allows, replace the bare entries in renderSettings with Write(env:POST_WORKER_WORKTREE/**) etc.; the unit test forbids dead path-scoped entries today so the change must be re-proven first.
notes_for_supervisor: RESULT normalised by the Supervisor into the published schema: the worker emitted tests[].output instead of .evidence and acceptance[] as plain strings. No content was dropped; the raw artifact is preserved as RESULT.worker-raw.json. Acceptance statuses are the SUPERVISOR's G2 verdicts, not the worker's. Root cause is a harness gap: spawn.sh never passed --json-schema to claude, so the result contract was prose-only with no machine enforcement (T0011 must close this). Original notes: Two production bugs were found only because the CLI tests use a real separate process: gitOutput stringified *exec.ExitError with %s (branchExists could never see exit 1, breaking worktree creation on any repo without the task branch), and the --timeout wrapper was passed to claude as its first argument (timed-out workers would never be killed). Both fixed with regression assertions.
